jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Job Title: Director of Finance

Job Type: 3-Month Contract (Possibility to convert), 5 days in-office, Calgary, AB

Job Salary: $80 - $90 / hour

JOB DESCRIPTION

·Provide financial leadership, governance, and oversight across multiple Canadian operating divisions and business units.
·Serve as a trusted advisor to the executive team, translating financial information into meaningful insights that support strategic decision-making.
·Lead the preparation, review, and consolidation of financial statements, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow reporting across multiple entities.
·Maintain the accuracy and reliability of financial reporting through robust internal controls, policies, and financial procedures.
·Oversee full-cycle accounting operations across entities, including intercompany accounting, reconciliations, and consolidations.
·Deliver ongoing financial and operational analysis to assess business performance, identify risks, and support growth initiatives.
·Develop and refine sophisticated financial models to support land development initiatives, capital planning activities, and investment evaluations.
·Manage weekly and monthly cash flow forecasting processes and support effective capital deployment across projects and geographic regions.
·Collaborate closely with leaders in development, construction, and sales to ensure alignment between financial objectives and business priorities.
·Direct the year-end financial reporting process and act as the primary point of contact for external audit engagements.
·Build, mentor, and lead a strong finance team by fostering accountability, professional development, and operational excellence.
·Provide financial guidance and support for strategic initiatives, acquisitions, business integrations, and expansion opportunities.

Role Requirements

·CPA designation is required.
·10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership responsibility within multi-entity or multi-division environments.
·Prior experience within land development, real estate, construction, or a closely related industry is required.
·Solid understanding of project-based accounting, capital budgeting, development pro formas, and financial planning processes.
·Demonstrated experience with financial consolidations, intercompany transactions, and complex multi-entity reporting structures.
·Experience working with ERP systems, along with advanced proficiency in Excel and financial reporting tools.

jobs.title: Vice President, Registry Operations
jobs.description:
Reliable registry services depend on more than strong processes. They take leaders who bring people, systems and resources together to deliver accurate, accessible service—and who turn improvement opportunities into measurable results. If you bring that combination of operational discipline and customer focus, this is an opportunity to put it to work at ISC.

The Opportunity

As Vice President, Registry Operations, you will lead the efficient, effective and profitable delivery of registries, directories, tax administration and related services on behalf of government and other clients. As a member of ISC’s Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute operational and financial insight to corporate planning and translate approved priorities into practical operating plans, budgets and clear accountabilities.

Your mandate will balance service quality, customer experience, employee engagement and financial performance while meeting legal, regulatory, contractual and information security requirements.

What You’ll Lead

Operational excellence.
Lead day-to-day delivery across complex registry operations, establishing sustainable operating models, shared capabilities and consistent processes that improve accuracy, productivity and service reliability.
Financial performance.
Own operating budgets, forecasts and financial results. Align capacity and spending with service demands, manage costs and variances, safeguard corporate assets and take timely corrective action within delegated authority.
Customer experience and client confidence.
Strengthen service accessibility, turnaround times and responsiveness. Use feedback and complaint trends to resolve recurring issues, maintain effective client relationships and provide clear reporting on service commitments.
Contract governance and risk management.
Ensure delivery meets applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, service level agreements and multi-year Licensing, Service and Operating Agreements. Address disruptions, escalate material risks and follow through on corrective actions.
Continuous improvement.
Turn performance data into practical improvements. Build clear business cases, prioritize approved systems and process changes, and reduce duplication, rework and avoidable costs without compromising quality or compliance.
People leadership.
Coach and develop managers, clarify decision-making authority and establish ownership of service, staffing and budget results. Support employee engagement, positive labour relations and a collaborative, service-focused culture grounded in ISC’s values.
Cross-functional delivery and growth support.
Partner across ISC to align technology, staffing and support services with operational needs. Bring operational expertise to new business and acquisition assessments, and deliver approved integration plans within agreed budgets, timelines and service requirements.
Quality and information security.
Oversee effective quality management and information security systems, including ISO 27001 and other adopted standards, with clear accountability for controls, audit findings and corrective actions.

What You Bring

A post-secondary degree in a relevant discipline and at least 10 years of senior management experience in an organization of comparable size and complexity.
Strong business acumen and experience leading operations, improving customer experience, managing
client relationships and delivering on budgets, forecasts and cost-control commitments.
Senior-level knowledge of service delivery, quality systems, operational controls, capacity planning, service level agreements, project and change management, and continuous improvement.
A record of delivering measurable efficiencies and better customer outcomes while maintaining service continuity, meeting approved budgets and establishing clear accountability for results.
Working knowledge of human resources management, organizational development, employment laws and union labour relations, supported by an ability to coach managers and lead teams through change.
Experience in regulatory or regulated industries, along with the ability to interpret and apply relevant legislation, would be an asset.

What You Bring

You will help strengthen ISC’s reputation as a reliable registry and regulatory operator by delivering on client commitments, making services easier to access and use, and building operations that perform consistently. This role offers the opportunity to contribute at the senior leadership table while staying connected to the people, processes and decisions that shape everyday service.

Help shape how we deliver essential services, strengthen performance and build lasting client confidence. Bring your ideas, lead improvements that matter and help teams succeed in a role where your leadership will make a visible difference. If you’re ready to combine strategic influence with hands-on operational impact, we invite you to explore your next chapter with ISC.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca. Applications may be submitted confidentially through Leadership Source (https://pod7.app.loxo.co/job/NDM1NjMtZmF0Y3JtN3NhZzdkYjY4Ng==?t=1794850064238).

Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain - Canada
jobs.description:
Job Location: Laval, Quebec, CAN

Job Requisition ID: 15804

Join our global diversified pharmaceutical company enriching lives through our relentless drive to deliver better health outcomes to our patients. We are all in it together to make a difference. Be a part of a culture that doesn't just wait for change but actively creates it—where your skills and values drive our collective progress and impact.

We are looking for a trustworthy and respectful individual who consistently does the right thing. Someone who is imaginative and proactive, with a keen eye for what is possible. A perceptive and adaptive person who is action oriented. We need a disciplined, focused, and accountable team member. If you embody these values, come join our company and help us shape the future.

General Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Supply Chain Planning function across Canada. The primary objective of the role is to ensure reliable, customer-focused product supply while optimizing inventory investment, manufacturing capacity, and overall supply chain performance.

The incumbent is responsible for establishing and implementing integrated demand, supply, inventory, and production planning processes to support business growth, customer service, financial objectives, and the overall supply chain strategy.

The incumbent provides leadership to the Planning teams across two Canadian manufacturing sites, as well as the Commercial Planning team, which works closely and regularly with the business units.

The Supply Chain Planning function plays a central role within the organization, connecting commercial strategy with manufacturing operations and supply execution. The incumbent works closely with Business Leadership, Quality, Procurement, Manufacturing, Commercial Operations, Business Intelligence, Finance, Regulatory Affairs, Logistics & Distribution, Human Resources, and Global Supply Chain Leadership.

As a leader of leaders, the incumbent directly supervises five employees across three locations and is responsible for building organizational capabilities, fostering collaboration, and developing a high-performing planning organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Demand Planning function and process for Canada, ensuring the development of robust, data-driven forecasts aligned with commercial strategy and market dynamics.
Lead the Supply Planning function and process for Canada, ensuring product availability and appropriate alignment between demand, supply, production capacity, and inventory.
Oversee Inventory Management and Planning, balancing customer service, working capital, inventory health, and obsolescence risks.
Lead the Production Planning function across two Canadian manufacturing sites.
Own the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) and Integrated Business Planning (IBP) processes, ensuring alignment between Commercial, Finance, Operations, and Supply Chain.
Monitor and improve key planning and supply chain performance indicators, including forecast accuracy, forecast bias, inventory levels, obsolescence, backorders, and customer service levels, including fill rate.
Partner with Logistics & Distribution teams to optimize end-to-end product flow and ensure customer requirements are consistently met.
Contribute to annual budgeting, strategic planning, and quarterly financial forecast updates, including financial assumptions related to inventory and supply.
Develop and implement supply chain planning strategies that support business growth, operational resilience, cost optimization, and customer service objectives.
Identify and lead initiatives to improve planning processes, systems, data quality, and organizational effectiveness.
Participate in the Global Supply Chain Planning Leadership Team, contributing to global standards, transformation initiatives, and best-practice sharing.
Collaborate strategically with Commercial, Finance, Quality, Procurement, Regulatory Affairs, Human Resources, Logistics & Distribution, and Operations leaders.
Work closely with manufacturing sites to ensure alignment between production plans, manufacturing capacity, raw materials, and operational requirements.
Lead talent development, performance management, employee retention, and succession planning activities within the Planning function.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer-centric decision-making.

Education And Experience Requirements

A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related discipline is required.
An advanced degree in Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field is considered an asset.
A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant supply chain experience within the pharmaceutical, life sciences, or healthcare industries.
Demonstrated experience leading supply chain planning activities at both the manufacturing site level and across multiple sites at an organizational level.
Significant people leadership experience, including developing high-performing teams and building organizational capabilities.
Experience developing and implementing integrated, end-to-end, customer-centric supply chain strategies and innovative solutions that improve service, inventory management, costs, and operational resilience.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within a matrixed, multinational organization and influence senior leaders and stakeholders without direct reporting authority.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, SAP and supply chain planning systems.
Professional certifications such as APICS/ASCM, CSCP, Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent are considered assets.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (French and English).
Strong executive presence, with a demonstrated ability to clearly communicate complex supply chain issues and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

Total Rewards

The range of starting base pay for this role is $145,000 to $180,000. Actual starting pay will be based on a wide range of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, qualifications, education and location. In addition to base pay, this position is eligible for participation in our annual bonus program.

What We Have To Offer Employees

Annual bonus plan
Health insurance coverage upon start date
Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP & DPSP) for qualifying employees
Competitive vacation policy
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) for qualifying employees
Employee Recognition Program
Full-service cafeteria with weekly lunch specials; free coffee and tea
Free onsite gym
Free parking
Electric vehicle parking
Tuition reimbursement
Years of Service Awards
Employee Referral Program
Maternity Leave top-up

Version française

Nous recherchons une personne digne de confiance et respectueuse, qui agit toujours de manière intègre. Une personne imaginative et proactive, ayant un bon sens des opportunités. Une personne perspicace et adaptable, orientée vers l’action. Nous avons besoin d’un membre d’équipe discipliné, concentré et responsable. Si vous vous reconnaissez dans ces valeurs, joignez-vous à notre entreprise et contribuez à façonner l’avenir.

Responsabilités générales

Assurer le leadership stratégique et opérationnel de la fonction de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement pour le Canada. L’objectif principal du poste est d’assurer un approvisionnement fiable et axé sur les besoins des clients, tout en optimisant les investissements en stocks, la capacité de fabrication et la performance globale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

Le ou la titulaire du poste est responsable de l’établissement et de la mise en œuvre de processus intégrés de planification de la demande, de l’approvisionnement, des stocks et de la production, afin de soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise, le service à la clientèle, les objectifs financiers et la stratégie globale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

La personne assure la direction des équipes de planification de deux sites de fabrication canadiens, ainsi que de l’équipe de planification commerciale, qui collabore étroitement et régulièrement avec les unités d’affaires.

La fonction de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement occupe une position centrale au sein de l’entreprise, assurant le lien entre la stratégie commerciale, les activités de fabrication et l’exécution de l’approvisionnement. Le ou la titulaire collabore étroitement avec la direction des unités d’affaires, les équipes de la qualité, des achats, de la fabrication, des opérations commerciales, de l’intelligence d’affaires, des finances, des affaires réglementaires, de la logistique et de la distribution, des ressources humaines ainsi qu’avec la direction mondiale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

À titre de gestionnaire de gestionnaires, la personne supervise directement cinq employés répartis dans trois emplacements. Elle est responsable du développement des capacités organisationnelles, de la promotion de la collaboration et de la mise en place d’une équipe de planification hautement performante.

Responsabilités principales

Diriger la fonction et le processus de planification de la demande pour le Canada et la Russie, en assurant l’élaboration de prévisions rigoureuses, fondées sur les données et alignées sur la stratégie commerciale et les réalités du marché.
Diriger la fonction et le processus de planification de l’approvisionnement pour le Canada, afin d’assurer la disponibilité des produits et un alignement adéquat entre la demande, l’approvisionnement, la capacité de production et les stocks.
Superviser la gestion et la planification des stocks, en maintenant un équilibre entre le service à la clientèle, le fonds de roulement, la saine gestion des stocks et les risques d’obsolescence.
Diriger la fonction de planification de la production dans deux sites de fabrication canadiens.
Assumer la responsabilité du processus de planification des ventes et des opérations (S&OP) et de planification intégrée des activités (IBP), en assurant l’alignement entre les équipes commerciales, les finances, les opérations et la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
Assurer le suivi et l’amélioration des principaux indicateurs de performance de la planification et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, notamment la précision des prévisions, les biais de prévision, les niveaux de stocks, l’obsolescence, les commandes en souffrance et le niveau de service à la clientèle, y compris le taux de satisfaction des commandes.
Collaborer avec les équipes de logistique et de distribution afin d’optimiser le flux des produits de bout en bout et de veiller à ce que les besoins des clients soient satisfaits de façon constante.
Contribuer à l’élaboration des budgets annuels, à la planification stratégique et aux mises à jour trimestrielles des prévisions financières, notamment en ce qui concerne les hypothèses financières liées aux stocks et à l’approvisionnement.
Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement qui soutiennent la croissance de l’entreprise, la résilience opérationnelle, l’optimisation des coûts et les objectifs de service à la clientèle.
Cerner et diriger les initiatives visant à améliorer les processus de planification, les systèmes, la qualité des données et l’efficacité organisationnelle.
Participer à l’équipe mondiale de direction de la planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et contribuer à l’établissement de normes mondiales, aux initiatives de transformation et au partage des meilleures pratiques.
Collaborer de façon stratégique avec les dirigeants des fonctions commerciales, des finances, de la qualité, des achats, des affaires réglementaires, des ressources humaines, de la logistique et de la distribution ainsi que des opérations.

jobs.description:
A career as Senior Director, Software Development within the Distribution and Brokerage Support team at National Bank means exercising technological leadership in software development and solution architecture. You will contribute to the modernization of applications, the adoption of artificial intelligence-assisted development practices and talent development, while influencing technological orientations and working methods.
Your job

Lead developers and QA analysts involved in solution projects, evolution, and maintenance.
Ensure the quality of the solutions delivered, from needs analysis to production.
Supervise the design, development and choice of architecture throughout the software development cycle.
Evolve development, automation, quality, and continuous delivery practices.
Drive application modernization and adoption of AI-assisted development approaches.
Develop the talents of the team through coaching, mentoring and professional coaching.

Your team

Within the Distribution and Brokerage Support sector, you are part of a team of approximately 15 colleagues and report to the Senior Director. Our team is responsible for the development, evolution and support of strategic applications used in the advisory and wealth management activities. It stands out for its technical expertise, its close collaboration with business partners and its commitment to the quality of the solutions delivered.We operate in an environment where innovation, continuous improvement and the adoption of new technologies are important. This position plays a key role in the continuity of the team's technical leadership as well as in the evolution of our development and architecture practices.
Our hybrid way of working includes being in the office 3 days a week, with the option to work remotely the other 2 days, offering flexibility and collaboration to support your work-life balance.We prioritize a variety of forms of continuous learning to enrich your development, including learning in action, sharing expertise, communities of practice, coaching, and specialized training. The development of technical skills and leadership is an integral part of our culture.
Prerequisites

Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience in enterprise application development and solution architecture.
Mastery of the full software development lifecycle, including quality practices, automated testing, and continuous delivery approaches.
Experience managing a development team.
Demonstrated leadership in coaching, mentoring, and developing technical talent.
Expertise in designing complex solutions and supporting multidisciplinary teams.
Ability to guide the adoption of new technologies and evolve development practices in a changing environment.

Nice to have
Experience with React, Java, event-driven architectures, relational and NoSQL databases, and AWS, including enterprise application modernization and transformation.
Experience with TDD, SDD/Design First and AI-assisted development approaches, including automation, standardization and the creation of reusable components.
Knowledge of the brokerage, financial advisory or wealth management sector.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to work closely with our colleagues outside Quebec.
Required skills: Active collaboration, Bilingual Communications, Business Alignment, Cybersecurity, Decision Making, Digital literacy, Emotional Intelligence, Managerial Courage, Mobilization, Problem Solving, Strategy Execution, Team Alignment, Technical Debt Remediation, Technical Leadership, User-centered Design

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan

jobs.title: AVP, Data Science & Price Modelling
jobs.description:
Experience Aviva

Together, we are Aviva.
Our values — Care, Commitment, Community, and Confidence — guide how we show up for each other and for our customers. Individually, they’re words. Together, they define who we are.

At Aviva Canada
, we put people first, our employees, our customers, and our communities. We’re proud of a culture built on care, inclusion, and collaboration, where your voice matters and your growth is supported. We’re not just about insurance; we’re about making a real difference by protecting what matters most.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an AVP, Data Science & Price Modelling
to lead a talented team that's transforming how we use analytics, machine learning, and predictive modelling to drive profitable growth and better outcomes for our customers.

In this role, you'll lead the development and delivery of advanced pricing models and data-driven solutions while partnering with teams across Pricing, Actuarial, Risk, and Technology. You'll combine technical leadership, business partnership, and people development to help shape decisions, solve complex challenges, and advance Aviva's data science capabilities. You'll have the opportunity to influence how one of Canada's leading insurers applies AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics to solve real business challenges at scale.

If you're passionate about building high-performing teams, turning data into action, and creating meaningful business impact, we'd love to hear from you.

What You’ll Do

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of leaders, data scientists, and analysts, creating an environment where people can grow, collaborate, and do their best work.
Drive the development, enhancement, and deployment of advanced pricing models, machine learning solutions, and predictive analytics capabilities.
Partner with business leaders to identify opportunities where data science can improve customer outcomes, business performance, and operational effectiveness.
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations that influence business decisions.
Oversee model governance, validation, monitoring, and ongoing performance to ensure models remain effective, reliable, and aligned with business and regulatory requirements.
Champion innovation by exploring emerging technologies, analytical techniques, and industry best practices.
Work closely with Pricing, Actuarial, Risk, Technology, and Engineering teams to deliver scalable, data-driven solutions.
Drive adoption of analytical tools, models, and insights across the business to maximize value and measurable impact.
Help shape priorities, allocate resources, and deliver key initiatives that support business objectives.
Foster an inclusive and collaborative culture that encourages curiosity, continuous learning, and diverse perspectives.

What You’ll Bring

Undergraduate degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Actuarial Science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
10+ years of experience in Data Science, Machine Learning, Analytics, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field.
Proven experience leading and developing high-performing technical teams.
Experience delivering data science and analytics solutions that solve complex business challenges and create measurable value.
Strong understanding of predictive modelling techniques, machine learning methodologies, and model development practices.
Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and build trusted relationships across technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience developing, implementing, and managing analytical models and data-driven solutions.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect analytical insights to business outcomes.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts in a clear and meaningful way.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, with experience balancing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

What Makes You Stand Out

Deep understanding of pricing analytics, predictive modelling, and machine learning within a complex business environment.
Knowledge of the Property & Casualty insurance industry and the opportunities data science can unlock.
Success building high-performing teams and developing future leaders.
Ability to connect business strategy, analytics, and technology to deliver meaningful outcomes.
Advanced degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field.

What You’ll Get

Compelling rewards package including base compensation, eligibility for annual bonus, retirement savings, share plan, health benefits, personal wellness, and volunteer opportunities. 
Hybrid flexible work model.
Outstanding career development opportunities.
We’ll support your professional development education.
Competitive vacation package with the option to purchase 5 extra days off per year. 
Employee-driven programs focused on gender, LGBTQ+, origins, diversity, and inclusion. 
Corporate wellness programs to support our employees’ physical and mental health. 
Employee discount on home and auto insurance (where applicable).

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Who We Are

Great banking should feel effortless. The kind where things just work, the right information is easy to find, and the next step feels natural. At YNCU, we’re focused on making banking simpler, more intuitive, and more useful in the moments that matter. So instead of making people think about how banking works, we make it feel like it just does. That’s one of the ways we show care.

YNCU was created by working people and small business owners who pooled their money to make affordable financial services available to one another. They weren’t just customers—they were our founders. That spirit still shapes how we work today.

Innovation is part of our history, too. Credit unions helped introduce some of Canada’s earliest banking innovations, and that mindset continues at YNCU. We’re always looking for unmet needs, better ways to serve members, and simpler experiences that make banking easier to understand and use.

What You’ll Be Doing

In 2026, YNCU announced a new strategic vision guiding the organization into 2026 and beyond, marking the beginning of its next chapter of growth, clarity, and shared purpose. The strategy sharpens YNCU’s focus on the people who build, protect, and care for communities.  This direction builds on the credit union’s recent growth, including the integration of Comtech Fire Credit Union, and reflects YNCU’s commitment to relationship-driven, community-focused banking.  As part of this direction, YNCU will deepen member relationships through personalized financial advice, simplify the way members interact with their credit union across digital and in-branch experiences, and tailor products and services to better meet the needs of those who serve others every day.

Consistent with providing Your Neighbourhood Credit Union’s (YNCU) Members with the right financial services to live life, dream big and achieve financial success, the Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides strategic leadership and oversees the organizations operations strategy including retail and commercial delivery, marketing, brand, product, member experience, operational excellence and credit administration.

The COO drives alignment collaboration across YNCU by standardizing sales, service and operational practices, removing barriers to execution, and enabling shared business success.   This role accelerates sales performance through strong leadership, coaching and accountability and a culture of continuous improvement as well as operational excellence and regulatory compliance. The COO leads member operations including payments, operations and agent deposit processing.

In addition, the COO will oversee marketing, product and brand strategy across all channels for YNCU to deliver meaningful product and campaign leadership to drive member growth and sustainable business performance.

Leadership and Strategy

Actively and collaboratively participate in YNCU’s strategic planning process with the Chief Leadership Team and the Board of Directors and work closely with peers to develop and implement long and short-term plans to bring the Strategic Plans to life.  Be an advocate for internal culture, new initiatives, and transformation.
Provide strategic leadership and guidance to all functional areas of the Credit Union related to operational excellence and member experience.
Provide leadership to assigned Team Members through effective goal setting, delegation, and communication, and drive the achievement of goals in responsible business areas.
Ensure the execution of established goals with Team Members and monitor progress toward and sustainability of achieving set goals.
Conduct performance reviews as required, and formulate and implement corrective actions as needed
Facilitate the design of career development and training plans for each direct report to include coaching, motivation and support

Member Experience

Develop and implement a Member Centric business strategy to deliver outstanding Member experience across the entire Member journey.
Ensure a high quality, service-driven environment through service standards and initiatives that continuously enhance services for Members including the establishment and implementation of measurable performance benchmarks to gauge Member loyalty/satisfaction. 
Act as the Chief Complaints Resolution Officer for YNCU and act in any government relations activities on behalf of YNCU and own the Market Code of Conduct.
Champion and evolve the NPS program at YNCU, including target-setting and action planning.
Partner with our marketing team to understand Member insights and research and translate to meaningful strategies to continuously improve the Member experience. 
Lead sales enablement: supporting the Chief Member Experience Officer and Chief Commercial Officer and the distribution teams to deliver exceptional advice conversations to members.
Develop and support the frontline in the development of programs that support pipeline management, leveraging YNCU’s investment in Salesforce CRM.

Operational Excellence, Process Improvement & Project Management

Champion procedural enhancements, support systems, resources and activities that are focused on exceptional Member experience.
Provide first-line support to retail branch operations to resolve in-branch issues, business interruptions or management concerns.
Ensure operational policies and procedures and reviewed, modernized and have meaningful job aids and workflows for our staff.
Apply continuous improvement methodologies to YNCU’s operations processes and procedures.
Project management leadership for organizational projects or changes to ensure stakeholder management, resource requirements, timelines and budgets are met.

Marketing

Lead integrated brand and marketing strategy to support growth in membership, deposits, and lending.
Oversee digital marketing, campaign management, content strategy, and market research.
Build strong brand positioning aligned with the credit union’s cooperative mission and community presence.
Drive data-driven marketing and personalized member engagement.

Product Innovation

Work in partnership with retail, commercial and wealth channel leaders to share Member experience feedback and partner on product evolution and innovation to meet Member needs.
Lead business case development and feasibility assessments for new product initiatives.

Operations and Payments

Lead the Member support and payment services team to ensure efficient and timely service to our branch teams. 
Accountable for payment processing, investment administration, estate administration and all payment services for YNCU.

Lead the commercial and retail credit administration teams, ensuring timely and accurate support to commercial and retail distribution teams.
Keep abreast of ind
ustry changes as they relate to payments modernization and open banking. Participate and manage any changes to payment products and services driven by industry or third parties.

Other

Actively and collaboratively participate in the annual budget process to ensure alignment of department with YNCU goals and objectives and create effective business plans.
Facilitate risk mitigation and ensure compliance with all regulations pertaining to Member Services.
Stay informed of trends and changes in Member Experience, products and services and provide reports to the Chief Leadership Team. Monitor local, regional and national economic, financial, industry and political events which could impact YNCU.
Prepare reports, participate in meetings, with the Board of Directors and serve on committees as required, and represent and promote YNCU at external functions.
Perform other duties as required.

This position is for an existing vacancy within our team.

What we are looking for:

Post secondary diploma, degree and/or certification in business, finance or a related program, or equivalent business experience
Minimum ten (10) years of senior level experience in financial services predominantly in the areas of financial services operations.  Experience with retail branch network. 
Strong knowledge of the Credit Unions Act and Regulations, Credit Union By-laws and Policies
Working knowledge of applicable government regulations and legal requirements
Sound knowledge of economic and financial trends
Effective understanding and use of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
Must have a valid Ontario driver's license and reliable available vehicle
Must meet bonding requirements

The compensation offered to the successful applicant for this role will be determined by the candidate’s relevant skills and experience and internal equity. More information about our total rewards package will be available during the hiring process.

Reports to:
President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Job Type:
Regular Full-Time

Work Location:
Kitchener, ON

This position is eligible for hybrid work arrangement.

We welcome applications from candidates based in the Southern region.

What You’ll Love About Working Here 

At YNCU, you are more than an employee. You are part of a purpose driven team that strengthens local communities and champions the credit union difference. We believe banking locally matters, and every day our team helps members build stronger financial futures through personalized advice, trusted relationships, and community support.

As a people first organization, we are committed to an environment where employees feel supported, valued, and empowered to grow. Through professional development, wellness initiatives, volunteering, and collaborative team experiences, we invest in our people because they are at the heart of everything we do. Programs like our Good Neighbours Employee Volunteer Program and Monthly Staff Donation Draws give employees a direct voice in supporting the causes that matter most to them and their communities

When you join our team, you become part of a collaborative culture that values authenticity, growth, and making a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. Some benefits that will support you:

Competitive compensation and incentive programs
100% employer-paid health benefits
Wellness benefits and resources to help you thrive both at work and at home, including mental health support, fitness programs, wellness breaks, and mindfulness resources
7% Matching pension plan
Paid vacation and personal days
Ongoing learning, training, and development opportunities
A free banking account and preferred employee rates on lending and investment products
Recognition and community engagement programs
Paid volunteer opportunities and community involvement initiatives
Professional development and certification reimbursement

Employer Awards and Recognitions

Certified B Corporation® organization committed to social and environmental impact
2025 Southwestern Ontario’s Top Employers

·Prior experience within land development, real estate, construction, or a closely related industry is required.
·Solid understanding of project-based accounting, capital budgeting, development pro formas, and financial planning processes.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Registry Operations
new_jobs.description:
Reliable registry services depend on more than strong processes. They take leaders who bring people, systems and resources together to deliver accurate, accessible service—and who turn improvement opportunities into measurable results. If you bring that combination of operational discipline and customer focus, this is an opportunity to put it to work at ISC.

The Opportunity

As Vice President, Registry Operations, you will lead the efficient, effective and profitable delivery of registries, directories, tax administration and related services on behalf of government and other clients. As a member of ISC’s Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute operational and financial insight to corporate planning and translate approved priorities into practical operating plans, budgets and clear accountabilities.

Your mandate will balance service quality, customer experience, employee engagement and financial performance while meeting legal, regulatory, contractual and information security requirements.

What You’ll Lead

Operational excellence.
Lead day-to-day delivery across complex registry operations, establishing sustainable operating models, shared capabilities and consistent processes that improve accuracy, productivity and service reliability.
Financial performance.
Own operating budgets, forecasts and financial results. Align capacity and spending with service demands, manage costs and variances, safeguard corporate assets and take timely corrective action within delegated authority.
Customer experience and client confidence.
Strengthen service accessibility, turnaround times and responsiveness. Use feedback and complaint trends to resolve recurring issues, maintain effective client relationships and provide clear reporting on service commitments.
Contract governance and risk management.
Ensure delivery meets applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, service level agreements and multi-year Licensing, Service and Operating Agreements. Address disruptions, escalate material risks and follow through on corrective actions.
Continuous improvement.
Turn performance data into practical improvements. Build clear business cases, prioritize approved systems and process changes, and reduce duplication, rework and avoidable costs without compromising quality or compliance.
People leadership.
Coach and develop managers, clarify decision-making authority and establish ownership of service, staffing and budget results. Support employee engagement, positive labour relations and a collaborative, service-focused culture grounded in ISC’s values.
Cross-functional delivery and growth support.
Partner across ISC to align technology, staffing and support services with operational needs. Bring operational expertise to new business and acquisition assessments, and deliver approved integration plans within agreed budgets, timelines and service requirements.
Quality and information security.
Oversee effective quality management and information security systems, including ISO 27001 and other adopted standards, with clear accountability for controls, audit findings and corrective actions.

What You Bring

A post-secondary degree in a relevant discipline and at least 10 years of senior management experience in an organization of comparable size and complexity.
Strong business acumen and experience leading operations, improving customer experience, managing
client relationships and delivering on budgets, forecasts and cost-control commitments.
Senior-level knowledge of service delivery, quality systems, operational controls, capacity planning, service level agreements, project and change management, and continuous improvement.
A record of delivering measurable efficiencies and better customer outcomes while maintaining service continuity, meeting approved budgets and establishing clear accountability for results.
Working knowledge of human resources management, organizational development, employment laws and union labour relations, supported by an ability to coach managers and lead teams through change.
Experience in regulatory or regulated industries, along with the ability to interpret and apply relevant legislation, would be an asset.

What You Bring

You will help strengthen ISC’s reputation as a reliable registry and regulatory operator by delivering on client commitments, making services easier to access and use, and building operations that perform consistently. This role offers the opportunity to contribute at the senior leadership table while staying connected to the people, processes and decisions that shape everyday service.

Help shape how we deliver essential services, strengthen performance and build lasting client confidence. Bring your ideas, lead improvements that matter and help teams succeed in a role where your leadership will make a visible difference. If you’re ready to combine strategic influence with hands-on operational impact, we invite you to explore your next chapter with ISC.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca. Applications may be submitted confidentially through Leadership Source (https://pod7.app.loxo.co/job/NDM1NjMtZmF0Y3JtN3NhZzdkYjY4Ng==?t=1794850064238).

Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.
